facts.text: Alila Manggis is a seaside resort in Manggis, East Bali, set amid a coconut grove between the sea and Mount Agung.
facts.excerpt: Alila Manggis is a secluded, stylish seaside resort in Manggis, East Bali. Set amid a coconut grove, the resort nestles between the sea and the majestic Mount Agung, Bali’s most sacred mountain.

facts.text: All rooms and suites face the ocean, with views across the straits to Nusa Penida.
facts.excerpt: All rooms and suites face the ocean with clear views across the straits to Nusa Penida.

facts.text: The resort's design is a contemporary interpretation of traditional Balinese architecture.
facts.excerpt: A contemporary interpretation of traditional Balinese architecture is artfully combined with modern amenities

facts.text: Rooms and suites are housed in traditional two-storey thatched Balinese pavilions angled to the beach.
facts.excerpt: Housed in traditional two-storey thatched Balinese pavilions, all 55 of our rooms and suites are angled to the beach for clear ocean views and seaside tranquility

facts.text: The Seaside King Suite is the resort's largest accommodation.
facts.excerpt: Go for the Seaside King Suite, the resort’s largest and most sophisticated dwelling at 1,220 square feet.

facts.text: Deluxe Rooms are on the upper floor with a private balcony and daybed, looking across the coconut grove, pool and sea.
facts.excerpt: Our 34 SQM Deluxe Room is located on the upper floor and offers the best views across the coconut grove, swimming pool, and sea.

facts.text: Spa Alila treatments take place in open-air bales facing the sea, shaded by pandan groves.
facts.excerpt: Nestled within the shade of pandan groves and facing the endless sea, Spa Alila offers a sanctuary where nature and well-being meet. Treatments unfold in open-air bales

facts.text: Surya is a yoga shala overlooking the ocean on Bali's east coast, where the sun rises.
facts.excerpt: Aptly located overlooking the ocean along Bali’s east coast, where the sun rises, Surya comprises a 10m x 10m yoga shala.

facts.text: Seasalt's signature meal is the Megibung, a traditional East Bali shared feast served on a carved timber stand called the Dulang.
facts.excerpt: Savour the ceremony and ritual behind Seasalt’s signature meal, the Megibung. In the customary tradition of sharing food with friends and family during village festivals and ceremonies in East Bali

facts.text: Seasalt serves Indonesian and Western dishes in a traditional pavilion set on a lotus pond.
facts.excerpt: Dine on vibrant Indonesian and Western flavours in a traditional pavilion set on a lotus pond at Seasalt, which offers all-day dining.

facts.text: Ocean Bar is an al fresco lounge and bar right by the ocean.
facts.excerpt: Nestled right by the ocean, the Ocean Bar at Alila Manggis is a cosy al fresco lounge and bar offering an extensive and creative menu of drinks and light bites.

facts.text: Roots of Tenganan is a cycling experience to the Bali Aga village of Tenganan, meeting master ikat weavers.
facts.excerpt: Cycle through emerald rice fields before entering this Bali Aga settlement, where customs remain untouched by the outside world. Wander among stone walls and woven offerings, speak with master ikat weavers

facts.text: The Flavors of East Bali cooking experience starts with harvesting ingredients in the resort's organic garden and cooking with a chef over a traditional firewood method.
facts.excerpt: Guests will participate in on hands-on cooking with Chef at the garden, starting with picking out the ingredients to cooking them together using the traditional firewood method.

facts.text: Caves and Crystals visits the Goa Lawah bat cave temple and the hand-harvested salt pans of Kusamba.
facts.excerpt: Then continue to Kusamba’s coast, where sea salt is still harvested by hand in sunlit rituals passed down through generations.

facts.text: Mountain to Sea is a cycling journey from the highland village of Selat past rice terraces and snake fruit farms down to a white-sand beach picnic.
facts.excerpt: Begin in the cool air of Selat, pedaling past rice terraces, snake fruit plantations and traditional villages. Descend toward the coast, where your reward awaits—a serene white-sand beach and a fresh-catch lunch prepared just for you.

facts.text: Alila Manggis received EarthCheck Platinum certification in 2023.
facts.excerpt: Achieving the prestigious EarthCheck Gold certification in 2016 and EarthCheck Platinum in 2023

facts.text: The resort runs a coral reef conservation programme with a local diving operation and follows a zero-waste policy.
facts.excerpt: the resort adheres to a zero-waste policy, conducts a coral reef conservation programme in partnership with a local diving operation

facts.text: The resort is about a 90-minute drive from Ngurah Rai International Airport.
facts.excerpt: Located just 90 minutes’ drive from Ngurah Rai International Airport

facts.text: Tenganan village, known for double-ikat Gringsing woven cloth, is near the resort.
facts.excerpt: Just near the resort, the village of Tenganan is renowned for its double-ikat or ‘Gringsing’ woven cloth.

facts.text: The Alila Leisure Concierge team tailors activities across five themes: Cultural Learning, Conscious Living, Active Spirits, Culinary Arts and Couple Celebration.
facts.excerpt: Enhance your holiday with lifestyle activities tailored to individual interests across five themes: Cultural Learning (love of history and artisanship), Conscious Living (wellness, environs and community), Active Spirits (outdoor sporting pursuits), Culinary Arts (cooking school and food trails) and Couple Celebration.

facts.text: Bicycles are available for personal use around the resort.
facts.excerpt: Bicycles available for personal use around the resort
